senses.gloss: (b. h.) [to be excited, confounded,] to err, do wrong inadvertently; to act under a wrong impression.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Keritot 4:1">Ker. IV, 1</cite> <he>ש׳ … באיזה מהן ש׳</he> if he had connection with one of them under the impression that it was his wife, and it is unknown with which of them.

<cite ref="Mishnah Keritot 2:4">Ib. II, 4</cite> <he>עשה בה את המזיד כשׁוֹגֵג</he> with reference to her the law puts the wilful transgressor on a level with the inadvertent (obliging him to offer a sacrifice).
<cite ref="Shabbat 69a:7">Sabb. 69ᵃ</cite> <he>ש׳ בשבת והזיד במלאכות</he>, v. <cite ref="G00277"><he>זִיד</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Shabbat 69a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>או שש׳ במלאכות וכ׳</he> or he acted inadvertently with regard to labors (not knowing that such a labor was forbidden on the Sabbath), but consciously as regards the Sabbath.
<cite ref="Shabbat 69a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>ש׳ בזה ובזה</he> if he was in error as to both.
<cite ref="Shabbat 69a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>עד שיִשְׁגּוֹג בלאו וכרת שבה</he> he must be ignorant of the prohibition (<he>לאו</he>) and of the eventual punishment of extinction <he>(כרת</he>); a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 146:6">Yalk. Gen. 146</cite> <he>מְשִׁיגִּין</he>, v. <cite ref="U00215"><he>שָׁגָה</he></cite>.
